# Report rules

<!-- generated by formal-sva 2.0.0; regenerate with `fv.py rules --design ...`; do not edit -->
Every report has a JSON document with a `schema_version` and a Markdown view
generated from it. Do not summarize only in prose.

Required artifacts:

| Artifact | Format | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `formal/spec/requirements.md` | extraction Markdown | spec agent / spec engineer + verification engineer |
| `formal/spec/requirements.json` | normalized extraction | deterministic script |
| `formal/reports/questions.json/.md` | clarification questions | spec agent / spec engineer / architecture / RTL |
| `formal/results/formal_results.json` | run results | verification engineer |
| `formal/reports/report.json/.md` | verification report | verification engineer |
| `formal/reports/junit.xml` | CI result | CI |
| `formal/reports/sva_review.json/.md` | SVA and constraint review | verification engineer |
| `formal/reports/regression.json/.md` | regression comparison | CI / reviewer |
| `formal/reports/regression-junit.xml` | CI regression result | CI |

Rules:

1. Every property row carries requirement, kind, role, depth, phase results,
   status, elapsed time and evidence.
2. Every failure carries a triage sentence and the counterexample or log path.
3. Unformalized requirements are listed explicitly; they never disappear into
   a percentage.
4. `BMC_PASS`, `PROVEN`, `COVERED`, `ASSUMED`, `UNREACHABLE` and `VACUOUS` are
   distinct words with distinct meanings.
5. Questions name an owner and a blocking decision. An answered question stays
   in the JSON with its answer.
6. Markdown tables are stable: column order does not change between runs.
